title: Shadow calibration + binary-search INT8 weight-only profile rollout and regression plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Integrate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles into a shadow calibration and regression pipeline. The goal is to validate accuracy and latency for a representative set of conversational and instruction-following models using a binary-search calibration sweep before promoting profiles into canary and production regression suites.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly CI job that runs binary-search calibration sweep for selected models (min 10k tokens per model)
Shadow deployment route that compares int8->fp32 outputs and collects per-prompt delta metrics (EMBED/LMscore/ROUGE-approx) and latency percentiles
Automated gating that flags regressions > 1.5% delta on primary quality metric or latency p95 increase > 30ms
Rollback and fallback playbook documented and tested with a synthetic canary
Telemetry shipped to console dashboards and automated alert rules configured
tasks: Define target model set: instruction-chat-small, instruct-7b, conv-13b (representative mix of seq lengths)
Implement binary-search calibration harness in quant-reports service (expose endpoints for calibration sweeps)
Add shadow route to serving runtime: route traffic to FP32 and INT8 weight-only variant in parallel, sample 1% production-like requests
Create nightly regtest matrix job in CI with seed corpus and token budget, output artifacts to s3://redwood-quant/regtests/73108
Create console dashboard with per-model accuracy distributions, token-level divergence histogram, and latency deltas
Add automated gating step that creates ENG issues for failures and annotates model/profile metadata
Document rollback steps and implement automated fallback policy in routing layer
risks: Shadow deployments could increase request cost and backend load if sampling rate misconfigured
Binary-search calibration may converge to profiles that degrade tail-case quality for long-context prompts
Telemetry volume may expose gaps in retention/aggregation leading to noisy alerts
Dependencies on calibration libraries (third-party GPTQ code paths) might introduce flakiness across GPU types
